content: The recommended dosage is 3 mg per day. Alternatively, a dosage of 5 to 10 mg can be administered three times daily. The maximum daily dose should not exceed 40 mg. Droxidopa therapy should begin at a dose of 100 mg and can be titrated up to 600 mg three times daily. Patients should avoid taking droxidopa within four to five hours of bedtime to minimize the risk of supine hypertension. Erythropoietin is administered subcutaneously (SC) or intravenously (IV) at doses ranging from 25 to 75 units per kilogram, three times per week. Methylxanthine caffeine is prescribed at doses of 100 to 250 mg, taken three times daily with meals. Pyridostigmine therapy is initiated at a dose of 30 mg three times daily, with a maximum allowable dose of 90 mg three times daily. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are rarely effective as monotherapy. However, they can be used as adjunctive therapy in combination with fludrocortisone or a sympathomimetic agent. Yohimbine has limited availability in the United States. Somatostatin is administered subcutaneously at doses ranging from 25 to 200 mcg. Ergotamine-caffeine (1 mg/100 mg) can be prescribed for patients with orthostatic hypotension, with dosing up to twice daily.
